reagents: acetic anhydride (1.5 equiv), pyridine (0.015 equiv, 1 mol % on the formylating mixture)
citation: Bax, P. C.; Stevens, W. Mixed carboxylic anhydrides. Part VIII. Synthesis of aryl thiolformates. Recl. Trav. Chim. Pays-Bas 1970, 89, 265-269. DOI 10.1002/recl.19700890305.
procedure: Bax, P. C.; Stevens, W., Recl. Trav. Chim. Pays-Bas 1970, 89, 265-269, Experimental section 2b ("Catalysed esterification"), which Table V states is how every thiolformate in it was made. Verbatim: "To 1.5 mole of F.A.M. (molar intake 2.0 : 1.0), containing 0.015 mole of pyridine, 1.0 mole of thiophenol was added. After 24 hours standing at room temperature the acids and anhydrides were distilled from the original reaction mixture under reduced pressure and at low temperature. Subsequently, the catalyst was removed by washing with water and the aryl thiolformate was dried over Na2SO4 and distilled." F.A.M. is the paper's name for the formic acid/acetic anhydride reaction mixture, made up beforehand by the method of its reference 5 (W. Stevens and A. van Es, Recl. Trav. Chim. Pays-Bas 1964, 83, 563); the thiophenol goes into that mixture, not into the two components separately. On the amounts: the paper counts the mixture by its acetic anhydride and gives the intake ratio 2.0 : 1.0 of formic acid to acetic anhydride, so 1.5 mole of F.A.M. is 1.5 mol of acetic anhydride and 3.0 mol of formic acid. Table IV lists that exact charge - thiophenol 1.0, acetic anhydride 1.5, formic acid 3.0, pyridine 0.015 - as giving more than 99 mole % thiolformate and under 1 mole % thiolacetate after 24 hours at 20 °C, and the paper's conclusion restates the conditions as room temperature with 1 mole % basic catalyst. Every quantity in this record is one of those mole figures; nothing is estimated, and the paper states no masses or volumes. The yield is the 87% printed for the S = H row of Table V, the paper's own figure for the material it obtained; a later paper (Polymers 2023, 15, 1647) cites this work for 90%, but 90% is a composition figure from Tables I and II for a different charge, not that 87%. The paper also warns: "Great caution should be exercised with the fractionation of the reaction products because in some instances the presence of the basic catalyst at elevated temperature caused decomposition of the aryl thiolformates." Physical data reported for this compound in Table V: b.p. 101 °C/15 mm Hg; n_D20 1.5862; formyl proton 10.07 ppm (PMR, TMS internal reference, measured neat); C found 60.9 (calc. 60.9), H found 4.4 (calc. 4.3), S found 23.2 (calc. 23.4).
